He played college basketball for the [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse Orange]]. ==High school career== Southerland played for Coach [[Ron Naclerio]] at [[Cardozo High School (New York City)|Cardozo High School]]. He participated in the 2006 Reebok [[ABCD Camp]] (N.J.). As a junior, he averaged 17.6 points, 11.3 rebounds and 2.6 assists for Cardozo. Southerland helped the squad to a 22–5 record. For 2008–09, he moved to Notre Dame Prep. He was rated 87th among the Class of 2009 small forwards by Scouts Inc.{{cite web|title=JAMES SOUTHERLAND - 2012-13 MEN'S BASKETBALL|url=http://www.suathletics.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=9474|work=suathletics.com|access-date=October 22, 2013}} ==College career== Over his four-year career, Southerland averaged 7.9 points and 3.3 rebounds while shooting .449 from the field and .370 from three-point range in 112 games. With nine, he tied the school record for made threes in a single game, at Arkansas, on November 30, 2012, while scoring a career-best 35 points.{{cite web|title=James Southerland's 35 points vs Arkansas were the 10th-most in the Jim Boeheim era|date=December 2012 |url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/12/james_southerlands_35_points_v.html|access-date=October 29, 2013}} Was named Big East Player of the Week on December 3, 2012.{{cite web|title=Syracuse's James Southerland named Big East Player of the Week|date=4 December 2012 |url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/12/syracuses_james_southerland_na.html|publisher=Syracuse.com|access-date=October 30, 2013}} On January 11, 2013, in his final season at Syracuse, Southerland was declared ineligible due to an undisclosed academic issue. He was reinstated on February 10, after missing six games.{{cite web|title=Syracuse basketball senior James Southerland wins appeal|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/02/syracuse_senior_james_southerl_1.html|work=Syracuse.com|date=February 10, 2013|access-date=October 22, 2013}} On [[senior night]] at the Carrier Dome, he recorded his first collegiate double-double, by scoring 22 points and grabbing 10 rebounds, against DePaul.{{cite web|title=In his first start of the season, Syracuse's James Southerland responds with first career double-double|date=7 March 2013 |url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/03/post_3.html|publisher=Syracuse.com|access-date=October 30, 2013}} During the [[2013 Big East men's basketball tournament|2013 Big East tournament]], Southerland set records for most three-pointers made in a game without a miss (6 vs Pittsburgh) and total number of threes made (20) in a single tournament, while being named to the All-Tournament team. Was selected as a member of the East Regional All-Tournament team during the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013 NCAA tournament]].{{cite web|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1587043-syracuse-vs-marquette-live-score-highlights-and-elite-8-game-reaction|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130402014708/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1587043-syracuse-vs-marquette-live-score-highlights-and-elite-8-game-reaction|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 2, 2013|title=Syracuse vs. Marquette: Live Score, Highlights and Elite 8 Game Reaction|publisher=Bleacher Report}} ===College statistics=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2013 NBA draft]], Southerland played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in the Orlando Summer League and the [[Golden State Warriors]] in the [[2013 NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.usbasket.com/player/James-Southerland/187084|title=James Southerland|work=usbasket.com|access-date=March 29, 2023|url-access=subscription}} On September 5, 2013, he signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets|Charlotte Bobcats]].[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-free-agent-forward-james-southerland Bobcats Sign Free Agent Forward James Southerland] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130908232005/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-sign-free-agent-forward-james-southerland |date=2013-09-08 }} He was waived by the Bobcats on December 11, 2013, after playing in just one game.[http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/cats-sign-douglas-roberts-waive-southerland Cats Sign Douglas-Roberts, Waive Southerland] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213074208/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/cats-sign-douglas-roberts-waive-southerland |date=2013-12-13 }} He was acquired by the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]] of the [[NBA D-League]] eight days later[http://www.nba.com/dleague/losangeles/131219_southerland.html D-Fenders Acquire James Southerland] and earned All-Rookie Second Team honors for the 2023–14 season. On April 11, 2014, he signed with the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] for the rest of the [[2013–14 NBA season|NBA season]].[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-sign-southerland PELICANS SIGN SOUTHERLAND] Southerland played for the Pelicans in the [[2014 NBA Summer League]] and then spent the pre-season with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].[http://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-announce-training-camp-roster Trail Blazers Announce Training Camp Roster][http://www.oregonlive.com/blazers/index.ssf/2014/10/trail_blazers_place_james_southerland_on_waivers.html Trail Blazers place James Southerland on waivers] Between October 2014 and December 2014, Southerland played in France for [[Limoges CSP]].[http://www.limogescsp.com/csp-pro-actualites-details/items/james-southerland-sengage-avec-le-limoges-csp.html James SOUTHERLAND s’engage avec le Limoges CSP] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023054901/http://www.limogescsp.com/csp-pro-actualites-details/items/james-southerland-sengage-avec-le-limoges-csp.html |date=2016-10-23 }} {{in lang|fr}} After playing in the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] for the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Southerland moved to Italy to play for [[Guerino Vanoli Basket|Vanoli Cremona]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/171768/vanoli-cremona-announces-james-southerland.html Vanoli Cremona announces James Southerland] On January 15, 2016, he parted ways with Cremona after averaging 5.1 points and 3.6 rebounds in fourteen games.[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/187988/vanoli-cremona-james-southerland-part-ways.html Vanoli Cremona, James Southerland part ways] Two days later, he signed with [[Mitteldeutscher BC]] of the [[Basketball Bundesliga]] for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/188131/mbc-announces-james-southerland.html MBC announces James Southerland] He averaged 13.5 points per game for Mitteldeutscher. Southerland returned to Germany for the 2016–17 season, playing 11 games for [[s.Oliver Würzburg]] on a two-month contract.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/212088/soliver-wuerzburg-signs-james-southerland.html S.Oliver Wuerzburg signs James Southerland][http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/219527/soliver-wuerzburg-james-southerland-part-ways.html S.Oliver Wuerzburg, James Southerland part ways] He joined the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]] in December 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/santa-cruz-warriors-acquire-james-southerland/n-5221522|title=Santa Cruz Warriors Acquire James Southerland|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=December 11, 2016|access-date=December 12, 2016}} Following the G League season, he had a six-game stint in Puerto Rico for [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]]. After playing in the [[2017 NBA Summer League]] for the [[Utah Jazz]], Southerland returned to the Santa Cruz Warriors for the 2017–18 season. On February 13, 2018, he was traded to the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web|date=February 13, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2018|website=GLeague.NBA.com|author=Camarena, Noah|title=South Bay Lakers acquire James Southerland, rights to Scott Wood from Santa Cruz|url=http://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-james-southerland-rights-scott-wood-santa-cruz/|archive-date=February 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180215084342/http://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-acquire-james-southerland-rights-scott-wood-santa-cruz/|url-status=dead}} For the 2018–19 season, Southerland moved to Japan to play for [[SeaHorses Mikawa]]. In December 2019, Southerland returned to Japan to play out the 2019–20 season with [[Yokohama B-Corsairs]]. In January 2022, Southerland joined [[CAB Madeira]] of the [[Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol]].{{cite web |last1=Xufre |first1=Ricardo |title=CAB Madeira tabs James Southerland, ex Yokohama BC |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Portugal/news/726741/CAB-Madeira-tabs-James-Southerland,-ex-Yokohama-BC |website=Eurobasket |access-date=January 15, 2022 |date=January 15, 2022}} In September 2022, Southerland joined the [[NBA G League Ignite]] for the [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–23 season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/ignite-announces-veteran-roster-additions/n-5885964|title=Ignite Announces Veteran Roster Additions|website=oursportscentral.com|date=September 28, 2022|access-date=September 28, 2022}} On March 28, 2023, Southerland signed with the [[Wellington Saints]] for the [[2023 New Zealand NBL season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.saints.co.nz/news/article/james-southerland-iii-joins-the-team|title=James Southerland III Joins The Team|website=saints.co.nz|date=March 28, 2023|access-date=March 29, 2023}} He appeared in one game before being released on April 19 due to injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.saints.co.nz/news/article/james-southerland-iii-released|title=James Southerland III
